title: Data residency & region pinning - security review
summary: Customer is a US-based digital health provider evaluating Redwood for handling PHI-adjacent workloads. Primary concerns: strict data residency (US/EU partitioning), region pinning for low-latency, cross-border processing, sub-processor disclosures, and KMS/encryption controls. Redwood AE/SE walked through hosted vs dedicated/private options, region pinning mechanics, audit logs, and SOC 2/ISO artifacts. Agreed next steps: share SOC2/ISO reports, region pinning tech note, and sample contract language; schedule follow-up to validate audit log schema and run a short benchmark in EU region.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-20 11:00 AM PT | Duration: ~55 mins | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Alex (Redwood CSM) — Anna (CISO), Mark (CTO), Elena (Legal), Samir (Platform)

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro: I'm Jordan Lee, AE at Redwood, and Priya our SE will cover the technical pieces. Alex is on for follow up.
00:12 Anna: Hi all, thanks. We're doing a security/compliance pass for any vendor that will touch our clinical metadata, so want to focus on residency and encryption.
00:25 Jordan: Totally. High level, we support hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity, and private deployments — with region pinning options for hosted and dedicated. Priya, do you want the deep dive?
00:34 Priya: Sure. So region pinning is our routing policy — you can pin requests from certain customers or routes to a geo-region, e.g., us-east, eu-west. For EU pinning we ensure compute and storage are kept in-scope; logs can be configured to remain in-region but there are minor caveats — I'll explain.
00:52 Mark: Caveats like? Are you doing any cross-border processing for model updates or telemetry? We need to avoid any PHI leaving the EU for EMR use cases.
01:04 Priya: Right. For hosted, model artifacts live in our catalog — those are not customer data — but telemetry, usage metrics and some metadata for routing can be processed in a control plane which currently operates in US and EU. We do provide a private control plane for customers that need full separation. The hosted default may surface minimal routing metadata cross-border unless you choose private.
01:28 Samir: When you say "control plane", is that metadata like timestamps, request IDs? We need to ensure no message text or PII crosses borders.
01:38 Priya: Correct — message text is kept in-region if you pin to EU. The control plane may have routing metadata. We also have a Dedicated option where you get reserved GPU pools in the selected region and we can disable cross-region telemetry. There was a previous doc where we call out what telemetry fields are sent — we'll attach that.
01:58 Elena: On sub-processors — we need a list of subprocessors for the EU region, and confirmation of notification windows for new sub-processors. Also standard SCCs and data processing agreement?
02:12 Jordan: Yes, SCCs are standard; we have DPA templates and a sub-processor list. We notify customers 30 days before onboarding new sub-processors in their region unless it's a security patch.
02:25 Anna: SOC 2 and ISO — are those available? How recent?
02:31 Jordan: We can share our SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certificates — most recent audits were Q2 2026. We'll upload the redacted reports — Priya can point you to the secure share.
02:45 Priya: Also, about keys — we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations. For private deployments you can use your HSM; for Hosted we offer CMEK through cloud KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, Google KMS). Note that for hosted CMEK we still manage the key usage through an access pattern, but customer controls key rotation and revocation.
03:12 Mark: If the key is revoked, does that stop tokens from being read in storage? How granular is the encryption — per-tenant, per-object?
03:20 Priya: We encrypt at rest per-tenant using envelope encryption. The object storage uses customer-key wrapping for the tenant key. Revoking the KMS key prevents decryption of future retrievals — there's a process we'll document. For Dedicated/Private you can keep keys entirely in your KMS/HSM so Redwood never has access.
03:44 Samir: Audit logs — what fields are available? We need request payload hashes, timestamps, route, model id, who accessed, and fulltrace ids for debugging. No raw messages in exported logs for EU pinned workloads.
03:58 Priya: Our audit logs include request id, route, model version, user id, timestamp, latency, outcome, and optionally a content-hash (we do a sha256 over the payload) rather than storing plaintext. For EU pinned setups we can redact or omit plaintext in the log exports.
04:18 Elena: Will you provide log retention policies and the ability for us to pull logs into our SIEM? SAML SSO mapping into RBAC?
04:28 Jordan: Yes, we have log exports to customer S3 or to streaming endpoints. SSO: SAML/Okta/Azure AD supported. RBAC is role-based — admin, developer, observer — and can be mapped from SAML attributes.
04:41 Anna: What about cross-border backups and snapshots? Are EBS snapshots or object-store copies replicated across regions?
04:50 Priya: For hosted the default is not to replicate backups cross-region for pinned workloads. However, some infra backups (control plane global backups) live in our backup region; for high compliance we recommend Dedicated or Private which keep snapshots local. We'll share the backup and snapshot topology diagram.
05:10 Mark: Is there any human review? If you have content review for model ops, does that ever route content to human teams? We need to ensure no manual review of PHI content.
05:22 Priya: We don't perform manual review of customer prompt/text by default. If a customer opts into content moderation or a managed eval project, that would be agreed separately and we can ensure it doesn't include PHI.
05:34 Speaker 6: (softly) mm-hmm.
05:38 Jordan: Pricing/ops note: Dedicated/private do add lead time and cost, but give you the strongest guarantees for residency and keys.
05:48 Anna: Okay, timeline — we're aiming to start a POC in Nov with EU-based subset of traffic. Would you be able to pin routes to eu-west and provide an isolated audit log for that traffic?
06:01 Priya: Yes. For POC we can set up a Dedicated reserved pool in eu-west or do a hosted-eu pin with stricter log redaction. For the POC we'd recommend hosted-eu pin first, then show Dedicated if you need stronger isolation.
06:18 Samir: For the POC, can we get a sample of the log export schema and a short runbook for key rotation?
06:26 Jordan: Absolutely. We'll send the log schema and key rotation runbook. Also include the DPA and sub-processor list.
06:33 Elena: Contract language — we may want a clause that prohibits cross-border processing of customer content for EU pinned workloads except for explicit exceptions. Is that acceptable?
06:46 Jordan: We can work contractual language; some of this depends on whether you pick Hosted or Dedicated/Private. For Dedicated, it's easier to guarantee. For hosted we typically carve out control-plane metadata, but we can tighten language for enterprise agreements.
07:05 Mark: One more technical: model updates — are those applied to the serving infra in EU or pulled from the global model catalog? We need to ensure model artifacts don't pull from US-only buckets during inference.
07:18 Priya: Model binaries are cached in-region for pinned deployments. The global catalog lives in our control plane, but the actual runtime binaries are fetched to region-specific caches. For pinned EU traffic we ensure runtime execution and KV cache stay in-region. Occasionally, metadata checks from the control plane may hit the US; we'll document that and offer private control plane for full separation.
07:44 Anna: Can you confirm subprocessors in EU — specifically which cloud provider regions and any third-party logs processors?
07:52 Jordan: We'll share the subprocessor list including the cloud region endpoints and log processor vendors; we do use a SIEM partner in EU for certain customers but that can be opted out.
08:04 Samir: Latency — pinning to eu-west gives us expected p95 latency figures? We need to know impact of strict redaction and CMEK on latency.
08:15 Priya: P95 for base text generation in eu-west on Dedicated for our 13B model is ~180-220ms token latency under typical load; CMEK introduces small crypto overhead ~5-10ms for object retrievals but not per-token generation. Redaction adds a quick hash step on ingestion — negligible in the critical path. We'll share measured benchmarks.
08:42 Elena: Next steps on legal: please send standard DPA, SCCs, and any model-of-interest processing clauses. We'll draft changes after review.
08:55 Jordan: Sounds good. I'll summarise action items now.
09:01 Jordan: Recap: Jordan to share SOC2/ISO docs, DPA, sub-processor list; Priya to share region pinning tech note, log schema, and key rotation runbook; Alex to schedule follow-up POC kickoff in early Nov; customer to review and provide markups.
09:20 Anna: Thanks all. No surprises — we'll aim to have comments back within two weeks.
09:26 Jordan: Great, thanks everyone. End call.
